maria: FWIW I noticed a small but consistent p99 bump on canary after today's allocator kernel-bin switch. Dropping notes here.
aj: saw the alert, thanks. numbers?
maria: baseline p99 for small requests (~<300 tokens) was ~11.8ms, after switch it's ~14.1ms. throughput and error rates unchanged.
ryan: ran perf and a short flame. Top hotspots look surprising: pretoken::normalize, host::memmove, grpc::slice_merge. Memmove dominance suggests extra copying.
sam: do we know which bin the selector picked? any layout/alignment changes?
ryan: selector rolled to kernel-bin v3.0 which bumps allocation alignment from 64->128 for the pretoken buffers. My hypothesis: extra padding increases fragmentation and causes larger memcpy during compact.
maria: timeline: selector flip 08:52, canary traffic ramp 08:55, alert 09:10. infra-bot reverted at 09:40 (manual rollback). We still have traces from the window.
aj: can you paste the perf snippet?
ryan: ```
Samples: 3.2K cycles
 38.7% pretoken::normalize
 24.1% host::memmove
 10.6% grpc::slice_merge
 8.9% kvcache::lookup
 3.5% other
```
sam: grpc slice_merge presence means more frame copies during streaming. Maybe more partial frames due to batch timing.
aj: reproduce locally? params?
sam: I replayed small-req profile: `./bench/run --profile=flame --concurrency=60 --seq=128 --reqs=20k`. See memmove spike.
ryan: microbenching allocator: when alignment=128, average pretoken buffer size increases by ~12 bytes (padding) and memmove counts up ~1.7x on the coalesce path. In-place compact reduces memmove by ~50% on the microbench.
maria: quick mitigation: 1) roll selector back (done) 2) try reducing batch timeout by 1ms to reduce partial frames 3) consider in-place compact to avoid memmove when no fragmentation.
aj: I'll run an A/B on batch_timeout -1ms vs baseline on canary and capture p95/p99.
ryan: opened a PR with an in-place compact prototype and unit tests. Local perf: memmove time -55%, canary replay p99 reduced ~0.9ms. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/1257
sam: KV metrics during spike window: route /v1/generate had hit=80.5%, miss=19.5% vs baseline 84.8/15.2. Slightly worse, could contribute to alloc churn. Sending heap and malloc traces.
infra-bot: Rollback of kernel-bin -> v2.9 completed at 09:40:12. Health checks green.
aj: A/B early: batch_timeout -1ms lowers p95 by ~1.8%, p99 unchanged after 5m. continuing run. :thinking_face: 
ryan: follow-up tests: 1) run allocator microbench across alignment values 32/64/96/128 2) add counters for memmove calls in pretoken compact 3) run end-to-end replay with KV hot/cold mixes
maria: agreed. keep fixes minimal for short-term. If in-place compact lands we should gate behind a feature flag.
aj: noted, I'll gate it. Also will collect grpc slice sizes pre/post for the A/B.
sam: noting GC traces show small bump in short-lived allocation counts during the aligned bin window. Might be related to extra buffer copies.
maria: TL;DR for oncall: root cause likely allocator alignment change from kernel selector causing extra padding -> more memmoves and grpc slice copies. Mitigations: rollback (done), running batch_timeout A/B, in-place compact PR prototype. Next: validate on canary 24h and run full perf regression suite.
ryan: I'll post microbench results and open a tracking ticket with benchmarks.
aj: thanks team. :thumbsup:
